claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a relatively homogeneous microstructure lacking distinct, finely dispersed Cu-rich precipitates.
Annealing at approximately 700°C for 1 hour in an inert atmosphere will induce phase separation in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The post-deposition annealing treatment will nucleate finely distributed Cu-rich precipitates in the high-entropy matrix.
Annealing will increase the volume fraction of Cu-rich precipitates relative to the as-deposited coating.
Annealing will produce a more uniform and refined distribution of Cu-rich precipitates.
Finely dispersed Cu-rich precipitates act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Finely dispersed Cu-rich precipitates inhibit localized plastic deformation during sliding.
Finely dispersed Cu-rich precipitates impede crack initiation during sliding.
Finely dispersed Cu-rich precipitates impede crack propagation during sliding.
The precipitate-mediated mechanisms mechanically stabilize the high-entropy matrix against shear and compressive stresses at elevated temperature.
The annealed coating will have lower wear volume than the as-deposited coating during sliding at approximately 600°C.
The annealed coating will develop shallower wear tracks than the as-deposited coating during high-temperature sliding.
The annealed coating will exhibit less subsurface plastic deformation than the as-deposited coating.
The annealed coating will exhibit fewer microcracks than the as-deposited coating.
At approximately 600°C, thermal activation enables precipitate formation and influences deformation mechanisms.
At significantly lower sliding temperatures, Cu-rich precipitate formation may not occur and the proposed mechanism may not be effective.
